name: GLM-5.2 + Open WebUI — frontier coding assistant on your own six GPUs
description: A private ChatGPT-style workspace in your browser, backed by GLM-5.2 running on six GPUs next to it. Open the service URL, create your account on the first visit, and chat — nothing to install locally and no third party sees the conversation. GLM-5.2 is a 744-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates only about 40 billion parameters per token, which is how a model this large answers at a usable speed: 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro and 81.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, the strongest openly published coding scores available, with a 262K-token context here that swallows a large repository in one conversation. Thinking is on by default and tool calling is wired up with vLLM's glm47 parser, so Open WebUI's tools and MCP connections work rather than coming back as unparsed text. HOW IT IS PUT TOGETHER: one container, one payment. vLLM serves the model on 127.0.0.1 only — the raw OpenAI-compatible API is never published, so there is no unauthenticated endpoint to find — and Open WebUI is the single exposed port. Open WebUI is installed at first launch into an isolated virtualenv on your bucket, deliberately separate from vLLM's own Python so its dependency pins cannot break the inference server, and it runs pinned to the CPU so all six cards stay with the model. AT LAUNCH select a persistent-storage bucket. There is no pre-configured account: the first account created in the browser becomes the administrator, and Open WebUI then switches signup off by itself, so open the service URL and register as soon as it is Running — until you do, anyone holding the URL could claim the administrator account. Accounts created afterwards, if signup is re-enabled from the admin panel, land as pending and see nothing until approved. The bucket holds three things that make relaunching cheap: the model weights, the Open WebUI virtualenv, and Open WebUI's own database, so your chat history, prompts, settings and account all come back on the next launch with the same bucket. FIRST LAUNCH IS SLOW AND THAT TIME IS BILLED: the weights are 753 GB and are fetched from Hugging Face before the model can load — roughly one and a half to two hours on a gigabit link, minutes on a fast one. Every launch after that reads them from your bucket. Buy a duration that accounts for it, and keep using the same bucket. REQUIREMENTS THIS TEMPLATE WILL NOT COMPROMISE ON, each checked before the download starts so a mistake costs seconds rather than hours: exactly six GPUs of at least 96 GB VRAM each, a large /dev/shm (the node operator must configure it — see the GPU note below), and around 800 GB free on the bucket. If any is missing the container exits immediately with a log line saying which.
outcome: Open a browser and chat with a frontier-class 744B coding model running entirely on your own six GPUs — history, settings and account persist across launches.

workflows.description: Not a workflow. This entry exists so the launch wizard offers the bucket picker: nodes-dashboard gates that picker on workflows[].length > 0 (templateNeedsBucketPicker in src/services/template-launch.ts). The bucket holds the 753 GB of model weights, the Open WebUI virtualenv and Open WebUI's database — without it the container refuses to start. The graph is deliberately empty and the container ignores COMFY_WORKFLOW entirely. Delete this once the node exposes a declarative persistence field.

requiredResources.description: EXACTLY six CUDA GPUs of at least 96 GB VRAM each, on one host, ideally NVLink-connected. Six is not a suggestion and not a minimum you can round up from: the model is 753 GB in FP8 and is split with tensor-parallel size 2 across pipeline-parallel size 3, which is the only layout that fits. Tensor-parallel 6 is arithmetically impossible here (the model has 64 attention heads, which 6 does not divide), and replicating the model per GPU would need 140 GB of a 141 GB card before any cache. At this layout each card holds about 125.5 GB of weights and keeps roughly 11 GB for KV cache — ample, because the model's compressed-latent attention costs only about 44 KB per token across all 78 layers. On six 141 GB H200s that is a comfortable fit. ONE OPERATOR PREREQUISITE: a service spanning several GPUs runs one worker process per card, and those processes exchange data through shared memory, so the node must give this container more than Docker's default 64 MB /dev/shm. The node operator sets this once per GPU resource via init.advanced (ShmSize, optionally IpcMode, PidsLimit) — see docs/compute.md, "Multi-GPU workloads". The launch script checks for it up front and exits with an explanatory log line rather than failing obscurely deep inside model loading. Open WebUI and its retrieval embedding model are pinned to the CPU on purpose, so nothing competes with the model for VRAM.
